title: Interleave-pulse benchmark diary — Caroline W.
content:
Purpose / quick notes:
- Small-request tail effects when small (<=64-token) interactive queries are interleaved with occasional long (>=1024-token) generation requests. Wanted to simulate mixed client patterns we see in beta customer A (chat + batch re-rank).
- Goal: measure p50/p95/p99 changes, throughput impact, and whether KV cache/coalescing preserves small-request latency under interleaving.

Experimental setup (staging):
- Cluster: 4x n1-standard-16 + 2x GPU nodes (A100-sim staging / dedicated staging pool). Redwood staging runtime v1.13.2.
- Model: llama-2-7b-v1 (quantized 4-bit) — representative small model used in demos.
- Client generator: custom loadgen (python) that supports Poisson + periodic long-job injection.
- Batching window: dynamic (max 12ms), baseline 8ms tuning.
- KV cache: enabled for short sessions. Measured hit/miss per-request.
- Arrival patterns tested: pure-poisson (lambda=200 qps), interleaved-pulse (200 qps small requests + 5 long jobs/sec, long job = 1200 tokens), bursty-surge (1s bursts to 600 qps every 30s).

Important commands / config used:
- run load: python bench/loadgen.py --qps 200 --pattern interleave --long-rate 5 --long-tokens 1200 --duration 1800s
- runtime flags: --batch-window-ms=8 --kv-cache-ttl=30s --adaptive-batching=true
- trace enable: /api/debug/traces?sample=1%

Raw numbers (median of 3 runs, staging, warm-cache):
- Pure Poisson (200 qps small-only): p50 16ms, p95 74ms, p99 135ms, throughput stable at 198 qps, kv-hit ~88%
- Interleaved-pulse (200 qps small + 5 long/sec): p50 18ms, p95 82ms, p99 210ms, throughput observed 195 qps for small requests (long jobs separate), kv-hit 73%
- Bursty-surge: p50 23ms, p95 150ms, p99 430ms, sustained tail oscillation after bursts for 12–20s
- Cold-cache interleaved run (restart between runs): p99 spiked to ~1.2s for a handful (~0.6% of requests) immediately after long job starts

Observations / interpretation:
- The p99 jump in interleaved runs seems correlated with long-job start events. Traces show kernel switch / CUDA context thrash coincident with long-job GPU kernels joining the queue.
- KV cache hit drop (88% -> 73%) explains ~25–40ms of extra latency for some requests (cache miss + full attention compute). But even with hits, queuing behind a long kernel increases tail.
- Adaptive batching helps average throughput but can increase small-request latency when long jobs cause batch composition to shift (small requests get batched with longer context, increasing per-token work).
- Warm-cache helps a lot — the long-job first-token penalty is the worst offender. After the first 2–3 long-job batches, small-request tails reduce, indicating some warmup at kernel/kernel-libraries layer.

Quick ASCII timeline (single interleave run, condensed):
[t=0s] steady small p95 ~70ms
[t=12s] long-job start -> p99 jump to 420ms (0.3% requests)
[t=13-16s] p99 returns to ~180–220ms
[t=30s] next long-job -> small spike but smaller (kernel warmed)

Hypotheses to test next:
- Hypothesis A: Kernel warmup / memory fragmentation when a long job's attention size causes different kernel path; if we pre-warm long-job kernels (shadow warmup), tail reduces. Test: inject a tiny synthetic long-job pre-warm 200ms before first long job.
- Hypothesis B: Batch composition anti-affinity: runtime is combining small + long in same scheduling window causing inefficiencies. Test: enforce batch-separation policy (no mixing pulses in same batch) and measure impact on throughput/latency.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache eviction policy too aggressive when mixed; measure per-tenant/ per-session eviction and tune ttl.

Actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run controlled pre-warm test (small pre-warm long job) with same seeds (run id: IPD-20250812-01). Assigned to Samir.
- [ ] Try batch separation flag in dev branch (PR 1789 references an initial prototype). Coordinate with Evan for infra rollout.
- [ ] Add focused tracing to capture kernel-selection decisions (file: traces/2025-08-12/interleave/). Caroline to add instrumentation hook.
- [ ] Re-run interleaved at 400 qps baseline to see scaling limits (danger: saturates GPU).

Notes-to-self / messy thoughts:
- Customer A traffic is not pure poisson; their client does 1–2 long ops per minute per user -> could aggregate to similar interleave shape we saw.
- Isolate whether long-job overhead is mainly first-token (scheduling + kernel load) or sustained (bigger token count). Early traces show biggest spike at first token.
- Might be opportunity for a lightweight long-job admission controller that staggers large context generation across GPUs to avoid synchronized kernel churn.

Links / refs inside run notes:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1789 (adaptive batch + batch-sep WIP)
- Jira: JIRA-INV-4823 (interleave pulse investigation)
- Slack: #eng-serving-runtime thread CK9Q12345 (notes from morning standup)

Short takeaways (for release notes / async update):
- Mixed small+long workload causes p99 degradation for small requests even when average throughput unaffected. Primary mechanism: kernel warmup + batch composition changes + occasional KV miss.
- Short-term mitigations: pre-warm long kernels, tighten KV ttl for these sessions, or enforce batch separation for small-latency critical lanes.
- Next: test pre-warm and batch-sep in staging; if promising, propose a low-risk rollout flag for Dedicated customers with low-latency SLAs.

Appendix: quick perf table (warm staging, interleave pattern)
- small qps	p50	p95	p99	kv-hit
- 200	16ms	74ms	135ms	88%
- 200+long	18ms	82ms	210ms	73%

End of diary entry.
